Daily flow on FWA segments, by day of a common year

Source: R/wet_segment_daily.R
wet_segment_daily.Rd

Reads mean flow per day of the year on Freshwater Atlas stream segments, by source, from wet's published discharge/fwa/v1/segment_daily (wet_catalog()): doy 1-365 on a common year, 29 February folded into 28 February. Each day is the mean flow on that day over the period, so wet_flow_window() gives a window's flow from the days themselves (basis = "daily") rather than from monthly means.

Usage

wet_segment_daily(
  conn,
  segments,
  source = c("pcic_routed", "wet_balance"),
  scenario = "historical",
  groups = NULL,
  catalog = NULL
)

Arguments

conn

NULL, or a DBI::DBIConnection to Postgres: the database wet_db_load() wrote to for from = "published", fwapg for from = "fwapg".

segments

linear_feature_ids. Repeats are read once.

source

Any of "pcic_routed" (PCIC's routed flow placed on the FWA) and "wet_balance" (wet's open water balance). Left out, every source from holds: both for "published", "pcic_routed" for "fwapg".

scenario

Scenario of the published product, e.g. "historical". fwapg's run is "historical" only.

groups

Watershed group codes that hold the segments: required when reading the parts (no conn), optional with conn. A segment outside them reads as missing.

catalog

For parts read without conn: the output of wet_catalog(), which is read when NULL.

Value

data.frame(linear_feature_id, doy, q_m3s, source), ordered by source as given, segment as given and day. A segment with no value for a source has all 365 rows, with q_m3s NA.

What the days are

For wet_balance the days are its published months laid out with a within-month shape fitted at HYDAT gauges (scripts/wb_shape_daily.R), so the mean of a calendar month's days is the month wet_segment_monthly() reads. For pcic_routed they are PCIC's routed day-of-year climatology, placed on the FWA by fwapg and routed and clamped at zero day by day, so where a clamp applied the mean of a month's days can sit above the published month. Neither has an annual row: month 0 is not the mean of the 365 days.

Where the values come from

From the Postgres table discharge.fwa_v1_segment_daily that wet_db_load() writes when conn is given, otherwise from the parquet parts the manifest lists, through duckdb. Each part holds one watershed group, so a read of the parts needs groups and opens only those groups' parts.

See also

wet_flow_window() for flow over month-day windows; wet_segment_monthly() for monthly and annual flow.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Buck Creek at its mouth, where gauge 08EE013 sits, from the published
# parts over HTTPS
q <- wet_segment_daily(NULL, 17094080, groups = "BULK")
wet_flow_window(q, wet_windows_calendar())
} # }
